summary: Adds Collect.isValid to check that a Collect's row type matches the type derived from its input, with a unit test.

tests.evidence: CollectTest covers only one- and two-column inputs; no case for a multi-column ARRAY/MULTISET query constructor whose row type comes from SqlTypeUtil.deriveCollectionQueryComponentType (uniquify), the path the reviewer showed was missed.

user_docs.evidence: Internal invariant check; no user-facing option or syntax.

doc_comments.evidence: Override of an existing method; inline comment explains the single-column case.

change_description.evidence: PR body is only the Jira link; the title states the change and the change is internal.

performance.evidence: isValid runs under planner assertions only.

backward_compat.evidence: A new invariant checked by the planner with assertions enabled could reject plans with hand-built Collect row types that were accepted before.

error_model.evidence: New litmus failure messages; they include the offending types.

correctness.evidence: Reviewer zzwqqq: the check does not compare against SqlTypeUtil.deriveCollectionQueryComponentType as Collect.create(..., SqlKind, ...) does, so a query-constructor Collect over a multi-column input with duplicate names (uniquify) is rejected; fixed in the second commit.

contradictions.evidence: The check duplicates derivation logic in Collect.create; the initial version disagreed with it, which is covered under correctness.

plan.why: Small cohesive change: one method and its test.
